correctness.rationale: The maximal domain follows from fixed-point existence for full isotone maps; finite order-preserving partial maps are nilpotent iff they have no periodic orbit and hence no fixed point. For each single omitted point, monotonicity forces every left orbit to move strictly upward toward the omission and every right orbit strictly downward. Reverse complement/shift give two independent nondecreasing parking-function sequences, with ranks counted by Narayana polynomials and common image value exactly the omitted point. Lagrange inversion of u=z(1+u)(1+tu) proves 2/(n-1)*binom(n,r+1)*binom(n-1,r-1) for every n>=2 and 1<=r<n. Independent exhaustive trajectory enumeration through n=9 and exact arithmetic identities through n=150 passed. Boundary n=1 is separately specified; finite checks do not establish the universal result.

originality.rationale: Primary full-text comparison finds no stated maximal-domain nilpotent image-rank distribution in the 2013 Laradji–Umar preprint, which instead proves distinct ambient/ordered-decreasing enumerations. Garba 1994 and Laradji–Umar 2004 are relevant but only their abstracts and citations could be read, so priority remains genuinely uncertain. 2015 subpermutation counts restrict to injective maps. The Narayana and Catalan numbers are known; originality concerns the extremal nilpotent semigroup interpretation, omitted-point factorization and closed distribution, not discovery of a number sequence. Comparisons with previously stated related scientific claims and published research search results did not reveal a covering implication; a search miss alone was not used as proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Maximal domain n-1 is forced by the fixed-point theorem for full weakly monotone maps and is thus an intrinsic extremal stratum, not a chosen arbitrary slice. Image rank is a standard semigroup invariant. The exact distribution and its missing-point refinement solve a natural extremal enumeration for every n, yield sharp rank endpoints and Catalan total, and expose a structural two-sided Narayana decomposition useful for conditioning on where nilpotent orbits escape. It is more informative than a known Catalan total or an isolated table calculation.
